newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Tiny Primagaz -MOL jv a hit-CEO.
newsitem.headline: Tiny Primagaz -MOL jv a hit-CEO.

text.p: The benefits of Alfagas, a small joint venture of Hungarian oil and gas company MOL RT and Primagaz far outweighs its actual size, Primagaz's CEO told Reuters on Thursday.
"Alfagas has exclusive gas transfer rights and we plan to increase transfers to 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes a year from 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes in previous years," Zoltan Szemmelweisz said.

The 60-40 MOL-Primagaz joint venture Alfagas, a three-person operation in the north Hungarian railway station of Zahony, transfers Russian gas shipments arriving at Hungary's border with the Ukraine in wide-gauge rail tankers to standard-gauge tankers.

"We not only handle our own needs as a priority, but also some transfer to other countries," Szemmelweisz said. These countries included Romania, Slovenia, Italy, Austria, Germany and Switzerland, he said.

Primagaz, Hungary's largest liquefied petroleum gas distributor, is 64.7 percent owned by Netherland's Pam Gas BV, which is owned by SVH Energy NV, a subsidiary of SHV Holdings NV. Osterreichische Kontrollbank AG holds 5.5 percent in Primagaz and Creditanstalt 4.2 percent. On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Primagaz shares closed at 9,995 forints on Wednesday.
